subject.title: WhatsApp QR-unavailable/headless login needs phone-code fallback

question: Should WhatsApp phone-code login be exposed through the generic channel login contract and `channels login --phone-number`, or should the entrypoint stay WhatsApp-owned?
rationale: The requested fix crosses a public CLI flag, plugin-facing auth contract, and persisted WhatsApp session-state handling, which is a product/API boundary choice rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Accept Generic Login Method After Proof
options.body: Keep the typed generic login method and `--phone-number` flag, but require the Baileys pairing-code fix, QR compatibility, upgrade proof, and live WhatsApp smoke before merge.

options.title: Move To WhatsApp-Owned Surface
options.body: Rework the active PR so phone-code login stays local to the WhatsApp plugin without expanding the generic channel-auth contract.

options.title: Pause Until Dependency Path Is Proven
options.body: Keep this issue open while waiting for stronger Baileys pairing-code proof or upstream hardening before committing to a public entrypoint.

recommendation.title: Accept Generic Login Method After Proof
recommendation.body: Keep the typed generic login method and `--phone-number` flag, but require the Baileys pairing-code fix, QR compatibility, upgrade proof, and live WhatsApp smoke before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: mcaxtr owns the newer open implementation candidate and is already working in the exact WhatsApp auth/session and channel-auth surfaces that need the decision.
